source_status: Digitized published observed curves, NOT original exposures or a released numerical table
measurement: Same lunar surface element's in-eclipse brightness divided by fully out-of-eclipse brightness
direction: Western umbra, 30 degrees north of equator, as labeled in Fig. 2
readout_definition: Half PDF stroke thickness plus 1 PDF point vertically; 1 point horizontally. Graph readout allowance only, NOT observational uncertainty or a confidence interval.

filter_information.method: pymupdf==2.1 full-text extraction of the fixed-SHA PDF, case-insensitive literal keyword search over body text, figure captions and table text; figure pages 3-5 additionally inspected visually

search.scope: full extracted text of all 5 pages (body, figure captions, table text); figure raster content covered by manual page inspection recorded in the task progress log
search.normalization: lowercase; hyphenated line breaks joined; whitespace collapsed; each keyword matched on three forms (as-is, hyphen-stripped, hyphen-to-space) so natively hyphenated spelling variants (band-width, response-curve) are covered; recorded count is the max of the three forms

filter_statements_present.quote: three narrow spectral bands with effective wavelengths equal to 503, 677, and 867 nm
SAO observations were conducted by two CCD-cameras with narrow filters with the effective wavelengths 503 and 677 nm.
Data obtained at 677 and 867 nm were also used to correct the effects of weak “red tail” of 503 nm filter.

filter_information.approximation_grade: Assumed rectangular and Gaussian passbands, FWHM 10/20/40 nm probe envelope; filter width and shape not measured and not stated in the paper
filter_information.upgrade_note: Requesting the measured filter response curves from the authors is recorded as an upgrade path only; no external contact was made

missing_information: Original CCD data and reduction products
Exact time attached to each curve coordinate
excluded: 867 nm is outside the present 380–780 nm baseline range
independence: Readouts sample smoothed published curves and are not statistically independent exposures
